tutorial.title: Using the Express Router
tutorial.descriptionContent: Dive deeper into the Express router by understanding how to use it to capture parameters and routes as well as how to use it to chaing routes

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
The router has a few more tricks up its sleeve. Let's look at how it handles route parameters.

router.param is used to capture named parameters from the URL, parse them, and attach the resulting value to the req object.

Make sure to pick router, followed by ., and finally param.

lessons.title: Lesson #6 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
As the first argument, we specify the name of the route parameter to capture. For example, a route parameter with the name "id".

Make sure to pick "id".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Pass a parameter name as a string in the first argument. Capture the parameter named id.

Make sure to pick router, followed by "id".

lessons.title: Lesson #6 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
The second argument in the router.param method is a middleware function.

The middleware function takes four parameters: req, res, next, and the captured value - in this case, id.

Make sure to pick "id", followed by id.

lessons.title: Lesson #6 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can use the captured parameter in the middleware to retrieve data, validate input, or attach the data to the request object for later.

Here, we'll simply log the captured parameter.

Make sure to pick "id", followed by id, and finally id.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can use a captured parameter to retrieve data, validate input, or attach data to the request object for later.

Capture the URL parameter id and log its captured value.

Make sure to pick router, followed by "id", id, and finally id.

lessons.title: Lesson #6 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Of course, we must not forget to call next to pass control to the next middleware or route handler; otherwise, the request will hang.

Make sure to pick next followed by ( and then ), ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
After logging the captured ID, pass control to the next middleware or route handler. Otherwise, the request will hang.

Make sure to pick next, followed by (, ), and finally ;.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Finish the code to make the router capture the route parameter name.

Make sure to pick router, followed by param.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Capture the parameter name on the router and handle only GET requests at /item/:name.

Make sure to pick router, followed by param, and finally get.

lessons.title: Lesson #6 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let the router capture the route parameter name so that calls to endpoints like "/greet/:name" will trigger the middleware.

Make sure to pick "name", followed by name, and finally name.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Let the router capture name from /greet/:name and log that captured value before continuing.

Make sure to pick "name", followed by name, and finally name.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
What method allows you to execute middleware when a specific route parameter is matched?

Using router.param("parameterName", middlewareFunction)`Using router.use("parameterName", middlewareFunction)`

Using router.param("parameterName", middlewareFunction)`.
lessons.hardModeContent:
What method executes sanitizeName when the route parameter :name is matched in /greet/:name?

router.param("name", sanitizeName)router.use("name", sanitizeName)router.get("name", sanitizeName)

router.param("name", sanitizeName).

lessons.title: Lesson #6 - Copy - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's missing here?

next needs to be called to continue with the request after the middleware executed its codeThe router should capture query parameters instead of route parameters here

next needs to be called to continue with the request after the middleware executed its code.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A request to /greet/Mia logs the name but never reaches its route handler. Which change fixes the shown middleware?

Call next() after logging the captured nameReplace the callback's name parameter with req.queryRemove next from the callback parameters

Call next() after logging the captured name.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does router.param("type") do?

It defines middleware that runs when a route with the specified parameter is matchedIt sets a static route for the parameter id

It defines middleware that runs when a route with the specified parameter is matched.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The router has /items/:type and /items/:id. When does router.param("type", loadType) run?

When a matched route contains the :type parameterWhenever either route contains any parameterOnly for the static path /items/type

When a matched route contains the :type parameter.

lessons.title: Lesson #6 - Copy - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Capture the parameter id with the router.

Make sure to pick router, followed by ., and finally param.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Capture id with router parameter middleware, log Capturing ID, then continue the request.

Make sure to pick router, followed by ., and finally param.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
Routers can also help reduce redundancy by allowing us to declare endpoints for multiple HTTP methods on a route, in a chained manner.

We do this by defining the route first via router.route.

Make sure to pick router, followed by .route, and finally "/book".

lessons.title: Lesson #7 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can then chain a GET endpoint to the route.

Make sure to pick get, followed by (req, res).
lessons.hardModeContent:
Chain a GET endpoint to the route, using a callback that can send the response through res.

Make sure to pick router, followed by get, and finally (req, res).

lessons.title: Lesson #7 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can add more endpoints if we want. Let's add one for POST and one for PUT.

Make sure to pick post, followed by put.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can chain more HTTP methods. Use post for POST and put for PUT.

For GET, send Get a random book. For POST, send Add a book.

For PUT, send Update the book. Make each endpoint handle its named method.

Make sure to pick router, followed by get, post, and finally put.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
Of course, we can use more complex routes as well. Create a route that uses a route parameter.

Make sure to pick / followed by item and then /, :id.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can chain methods on a route with a parameter.

Use /item followed by a final segment captured as id. Make the first endpoint a GET endpoint.

Make sure to pick /, followed by item, /, :id, and finally get.

lessons.title: Lesson #7 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can integrate middleware functions within the same route definition, allowing for preprocessing or validation.

We use all to run the middleware for all matching routes.

Make sure to pick all.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can add middleware to the same route definition for preprocessing or validation.

Use all to run middleware for every HTTP method matching the path.

Run the first function for every matching request, then run the second as a GET endpoint.

Make sure to pick router, followed by all, and finally get.

lessons.title: Lesson #7 - Copy - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can also define the middleware before and pass a reference to the function as argument instead of the callback function directly.

Make sure to pick logging, followed by all, and finally logging.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can also define the middleware before and pass a reference to the function as argument instead of the callback function directly.

Make sure to pick logging, followed by router, all, logging, and finally get.

lessons.title: Lesson #7 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
And of course, we can pass in multiple middleware functions. We can use multiple parameters or an array.

Make sure to pick logging followed by validateId and then all, [logging, validateId].
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can pass named middleware functions as separate arguments or in an array, in the order they should run.

Name the logging function logging and the ID-checking function validateId.

For every matching request, use an array to run logging first, then ID validation.

Make sure to pick logging, followed by validateId, all, and finally [logging, validateId].

lessons.title: Lesson #7 - Copy - Copy - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Last but not least, we can apply middleware directly in the chain as well if we want only specific routes to trigger it.

Make sure to pick logging, followed by logging.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can pass middleware directly to a chained HTTP method so only that method triggers it.

Name the function logging and run it before the GET handler for /item/:id.

Make sure to pick logging, followed by router, get, and finally logging.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
What advantage does chaining methods with router.route provide?

It allows you to define multiple HTTP methods for the same route in a clean and organized mannerIt reduces the need for middleware in the application

It allows you to define multiple HTTP methods for the same route in a clean and organized manner.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The path /book needs GET, POST, and PUT handlers. Which layout avoids repeating the path?

Chain .get(), .post(), and .put() after router.route("/book")Call router.route("/book") separately before each handlerPut all three handlers in one router.use("/book") callback

Chain .get(), .post(), and .put() after router.route("/book").

lessons.title: Lesson #7 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Add the fitting endpoints.

Make sure to pick get, followed by post, and finally put.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Add the fitting endpoints.

Make sure to pick router, followed by get, post, and finally put.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
Can you use middleware in conjunction with chained routes defined by router.route?

Yes, you can apply middleware using all or directly in the chainNo, middleware cannot be used with chained routes

Yes, you can apply middleware using all or directly in the chain.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Authentication must run for every method chained from router.route("/account"). Which setup applies it to the whole chain?

Start the chain with .all(authenticate)Pass authenticate only to the chained .get()Put authenticate inside the final response handler

Start the chain with .all(authenticate).

lessons.title: Lesson #7 - Copy - Copy  - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Pass an array of middleware functions that the router can execute every time the "/item/:id" route is matched.

Make sure to pick all followed by [ and then ,, ].
lessons.hardModeContent:
Pass an array of middleware functions that the router can execute every time the "/item/:id" route is matched.

Make sure to pick params, followed by router, all, [, ,, and finally ].

lessons.title: router.use() - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Routes can not only capture parameters but also routes to then execute custom middleware.

To execute certain middleware whenever a defined route is accessed, we need to tell the router to use it.

Make sure to pick router, followed by ., and finally use.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A router can capture parameters and run custom middleware for its routes.

To execute custom middleware whenever a defined router route is accessed, complete the router method call.

Make sure to pick router, followed by ., and finally use.

lessons.title: router.use() - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
The first argument of the method specifies the path that the middleware or route handler should match.

Make sure to pick router.use, followed by "/clothing".
lessons.hardModeContent:
The first argument of router.use specifies the path the middleware should match.

Configure middleware for /clothing and routes beneath it.

Make sure to pick router.use, followed by "/clothing".

lessons.title: router.use() - Copy - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Then, we pass the callback function that executes the middleware. Here, we log when a route starting with "/clothing" is accessed.

Make sure to pick (req, res, next), followed by =>, and finally console.log("Router use for /clothing");.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You pass a callback function to run middleware when a route starts with /clothing.

Log Router use for /clothing inside the callback.

Make sure to pick (req, res, next), followed by =>, and finally console.log("Router use for /clothing");.

lessons.title: daf
lessons.interactiveContent:
Of course, we must not forget next if we want to request to propagate further.

Make sure to pick next followed by ( and then ), ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
After logging, let the request continue to the next middleware or route handler.

Make sure to pick next, followed by (, ), and finally ;.

lessons.title: daf - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
The path of the route needs to start with the defined route to catch it. http://localhost:3000/clothing/info will be caught by our router.

http://localhost:3000/info/clothing won't be caught by the "/clothing" handler since it doesn't start with "/clothing".

Make sure to pick "/clothing".
lessons.hardModeContent:
With router.use, the request path must start with the middleware path to match.

Match /clothing and /clothing/info, but leave /info/clothing unmatched.

Make sure to pick router, followed by "/clothing".

lessons.title: daf - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can use multiple middleware functions as well when capturing a specific route.

We can either pass them as individual values or as an array.

Make sure to pick loggingMiddleware followed by authMiddleware and then router.use, loggingMiddleware,, authMiddleware.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can pass multiple middleware functions as separate arguments or an array.

For /game, pass logging first and authentication second as separate arguments, each once.

When a token is present, continue to the next handler after logging Authorized.

Make sure to pick next(), followed by router.use, "/game", loggingMiddleware, and finally authMiddleware.

lessons.title: daf - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Ensure the router captures the following route http://localhost:3000/movie/12.

Make sure to pick "/movie/:id".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Match movie URLs such as /movie/12 and /movie/34, capturing the final segment as id.

Make sure to pick router, followed by "/movie/:id".

lessons.title: daf - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Make the router capture all routes that start with "/book" and execute custom middleware in that case.

Make sure to pick router followed by . and then use, "/book".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Make the router capture all routes that start with "/book" and execute custom middleware in that case.

Make sure to pick router, followed by ., use, "/book", req, and finally res.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
How can you log all incoming requests to routes that start with /song using a router?

By using router.use("/song", middlewareFunction)By using app.use("/song", middlewareFunction)

By using router.use("/song", middlewareFunction).
lessons.hardModeContent:
The router should run logRequest for GET /song, POST /song/new, and other /song routes. Which setup works?

router.use("/song", logRequest)router.get("/song", logRequest)router.param("song", logRequest)

router.use("/song", logRequest).

lessons.title: daf - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Finish the code to make the router capture all routes that start with "/book".

Make sure to pick router followed by . and then use, "/book".
lessons.hardModeContent:
The route is already registered. Complete the middleware so it logs the request and then passes control onward.

Make sure to pick router, followed by .use, "/book", next, and finally console.log.
